chain.label: Kauai's mountainous terrain limits aviation safety infrastructure
chain.trigger: the mountainous terrain on Kauai and in other locations in Hawaii limits the ability of the existing infrastructure to fully support certain aviation safety-related functions

chain.label: Atypical weather front moved onto the tour route
chain.trigger: low clouds and rain began moving onshore from the northwest (which was an atypical weather pattern for Kauai) and affecting locations on the tour route

chain.label: Sparse weather infrastructure and ineffective FAA oversight
chain.trigger: air tour pilots in Hawaii rely heavily on their own in-flight visual weather assessments; ineffective monitoring and oversight of Hawaii air tour operators

caused_by.evidence: the mountainous terrain...limits the ability of the existing infrastructure to fully support certain aviation safety-related functions...air tour pilots rely heavily on their own in-flight visual weather assessments

chain.label: FAA never completed cue-based Hawaii weather training
chain.trigger: the FAA has not yet taken responsive action. As a result, the accident pilot did not receive the training we intended

chain.label: Safari lacked safety-assurance processes for weather decisions
chain.trigger: the company lacked a documented safety assurance process by which it could determine how effectively its pilots were assessing weather-related risks and adhering to company policy

chain.label: Pilot likely misjudged or was overconfident about the weather
chain.trigger: it is possible that he inaccurately assessed the weather conditions in flight or was overconfident in his abilities

caused_by.evidence: this atypical weather pattern may have increased the difficulty for the accident pilot to anticipate the weather conditions he would encounter
a lack of relevant weather information, which hindered his ability to develop an accurate mental model of the atypical weather situation
the accident pilot did not receive the type of training that FAA-sponsored research has shown can improve the accuracy of pilots' in-flight weather assessments

chain.label: Pilot decided to continue VFR flight into deteriorating weather
chain.trigger: the pilot's decision to continue flight under visual flight rules (VFR) into IMC

caused_by.evidence: his decision to continue the flight into deteriorating weather was likely influenced by...an inaccurate in-flight assessment of the weather conditions...or was overconfident in his abilities

Contributing to the accident was Safari Aviation Inc.'s lack of safety management processes to identify hazards and mitigate the risks associated with factors that influence pilots to continue VFR flight into IMC

chain.label: Helicopter collided into mountainous terrain
chain.trigger: collided into terrain in a remote, wooded area near Kekaha

caused_by.evidence: the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's decision to continue flight under visual flight rules (VFR) into IMC, which resulted in the collision into terrain

chain.label: Pilot and six passengers fatally injured
chain.trigger: The pilot and the six passengers were fatally injured, and the helicopter was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: collided into terrain...The pilot and the six passengers were fatally injured
